why_this_matters: 156 new entries in one day is the rate a new author competes against. It is also the number that makes any single entry's discoverability a function of time: an entry added today is one of 6,112, and the same entry in a month is one of roughly 10,000 at this rate. That is the argument for the vertical noun strategy — a name that matches a search, not a slot in a list.

our_entries_in_feed.note: every version matches the npm dist-tag, so the feed is not lagging the registry for our packages — the 13 pending entries are pending on merge, not on a stale npm map

category_distribution.note: all twenty of our checks sit in tools, the second-largest category. Fifteen more packages in this category buy no visibility that a search noun does not already buy.

reading: the catalog's shape confirms the earlier decision: ui is the most crowded and tools is second, so the differentiator is not the category but the noun in the description — which is exactly what each check's name and 搜索名词 were chosen for
